title: Section 5 (Bonus): Other Libraries for Working with LLMs in R
text:
NoteBonus content



We’ll cover this section if there’s time at the end of the workshop. It’s a quick tour of three packages built on top of ellmer: shinychat, querychat and vitals.


Download 05-other-libraries.R View on GitHub


code/05-other-libraries.R

# 5 - Bonus: Other Libraries for Working with LLMs in R
# Using LLMs in R with ellmer - LatinR 2026
#
# Bonus content - we'll cover this if there's time at the end.

# install.packages(c("shiny", "bslib", "shinychat", "querychat", "vitals"))

library(ellmer)

## shinychat - chat UIs in Shiny
## https://posit-dev.github.io/shinychat/

# A minimal chatbot: a chat_ui() in the UI, and in the server we stream the
# model's reply into it every time the user sends a message

library(shiny)
library(bslib)
library(shinychat)

ui <- page_fillable(
  chat_ui("chat")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  chat <- chat_openrouter(model = "anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5")

  observeEvent(input$chat_user_input, {
    stream <- chat$stream_async(input$chat_user_input)
    chat_append("chat", stream)
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

## The dog adoption assistant from section 4, as an app

# Same ellmer chat object as before - a system prompt, the dog listings, and
# the save_shortlist tool. shinychat just gives it a user interface.

dogs_csv <- paste(readLines("data/dogs_details.csv"), collapse = "\n")

prompt <- paste(
  "You are a dog adoption assistant helping the user choose a dog",
  "from the listings below. Keep answers short.\n\nDogs available:\n",
  dogs_csv
)

save_shortlist <- function(names, path) {
  writeLines(names, path)
  paste("Saved", length(names), "dogs to", path)
}

save_shortlist_tool <- tool(
  save_shortlist,
  "Save a shortlist of dog names to a text file",
  arguments = list(
    names = type_array(type_string(), "Names of the dogs to save"),
    path = type_string("File path to save to, e.g. shortlist.txt")
  )
)

# Welcome message with clickable suggestions
welcome <- "
**Hi! I can help you pick a dog to adopt.** 🐶

Try one of these:

* <span class=\"suggestion submit\">Which dogs would suit a small flat?</span>
* <span class=\"suggestion submit\">Which dogs are good with other dogs?</span>
* <span class=\"suggestion\">Save a shortlist of ... to shortlist.txt</span>
"

ui <- page_fillable(
  chat_ui("chat", greeting = welcome)
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  chat <- chat_openrouter(
    model = "anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5",
    system_prompt = prompt
  )
  chat$register_tool(save_shortlist_tool)

  observeEvent(input$chat_user_input, {
    stream <- chat$stream_async(input$chat_user_input)
    chat_append("chat", stream)
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

## querychat - ask questions of a data frame in plain language
## https://posit-dev.github.io/querychat/

# querychat turns questions into SQL, runs the SQL on your data with DuckDB,
# and shows you the query. Only the schema (column names, types, categories)
# is sent to the model - the rows themselves never leave your machine.

library(querychat)

dogs <- readr::read_csv("data/dogs_details.csv")

querychat_app(
  dogs,
  client = chat_openrouter(model = "anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5")
)

# Try asking:
#   "Show me dogs that are good with other dogs"
#   "What's the average adoption fee by age?"
#   "Which city has the most dogs listed?"

## Giving querychat more context

# Describing the data helps the model write better SQL. We can also drop the
# long free-text column so the schema is smaller. (querychat names the SQL
# table after the variable, so assign first rather than passing an expression.)

dogs_short <- dplyr::select(dogs, -description)

querychat_app(
  dogs_short,
  client = chat_openrouter(model = "anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5"),
  greeting = "Ask me anything about the dogs available for adoption!",
  data_description = "
    Dogs listed for adoption in the USA.
    age is one of Baby, Young, Adult or Senior.
    adoption_fee is in US dollars.
    other_dogs is TRUE if the dog can live with other dogs.
  "
)

## vitals - evaluating LLM output
## https://vitals.tidyverse.org/

title: Section 3: Extracting Structured Data
text:
The script for this section of the workshop. Exercises are at the end, under Your turn.
Download 03-structured-data.R View on GitHub


code/03-structured-data.R

# 3 - Extracting Structured Data
# Using LLMs in R with ellmer - LatinR 2026

library(ellmer)
library(dplyr)

dogs <- readr::read_csv("data/dogs.csv")

dog_description <- dogs |>
  slice(1) |>
  pull(description)

## The problem with unstructured output

chat <- chat_openrouter(model = "anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5")
output <- chat$chat(
  "Extract the name and adoption fee from this data

  ## Output format

  Name:
  Adoption fee:",
  dog_description
)
output
class(output)

## Extracting a single value

name_type <- type_string("The name of the dog")

chat <- chat_openrouter(model = "anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5")
chat$chat_structured(dog_description, type = name_type)

## Extracting a number

fee_type <- type_number("Adoption fee in dollars")

chat <- chat_openrouter(model = "anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5")
chat$chat_structured(dog_description, type = fee_type)

## Constraining to specific choices

age_groups <- c("Baby", "Young", "Adult", "Senior")

age_type <- type_enum(age_groups, "Age group of the dog")

chat <- chat_openrouter(model = "anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5")
chat$chat_structured(dog_description, type = age_type)

## Extracting a yes/no

other_dogs_type <- type_boolean(
  "Is the dog recommended for a home with other dogs?"
)

chat <- chat_openrouter(model = "anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5")
chat$chat_structured(dog_description, type = other_dogs_type)

## Extracting a list of values

likes_type <- type_array(type_string("Things the dog likes"))

chat <- chat_openrouter(model = "anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5")
chat$chat_structured(dog_description, type = likes_type)

## Combining multiple fields

dog_spec <- type_object(
  name = type_string("The name of the dog"),
  breed = type_string("Breed of the dog"),
  adoption_fee = type_number("Adoption fee in dollars"),
  other_dogs = type_boolean(
    "Is the dog recommended for a home with other dogs?",
  ),
  age = type_enum(age_groups, "Age group of the dog")
)

chat <- chat_openrouter(model = "anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5")
chat$chat_structured(dog_description, type = dog_spec)

## Processing multiple dogs

prompts <- paste("Extract data from this dog adoption listing:", dogs$description)

prompts

# parallel_chat_structured is a little different
output <- parallel_chat_structured(
  chat = chat_openrouter(model = "anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5"),
  prompts = as.list(prompts),
  type = dog_spec
)

output

## Combining them

dogs_details <- bind_cols(dogs, output)
dogs_details

## Save to a file

readr::write_csv(dogs_details, "data/dogs_details.csv")

## Your turn

# 1. Pick a different dog from the dataset
# 2. Extract the name and age group using chat_structured()
# 3. Process all dogs using parallel_chat_structured()
# 4. Bonus: Add a new field for the dog's energy level using type_enum() with
#    choices like "Low", "Medium", "High"

code/01-getting-started.R

# 1 - Getting Started with LLMs in R
# Using LLMs in R with ellmer - LatinR 2026

## Starting a conversation

library(ellmer)
chat <- chat_openrouter(model = "anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5")

## Sending a message to the LLM

chat$chat("What is the most popular dog breed in the world?
  Answer succinctly.")

## Your turn (1)

# 1. If you haven't yet: save your API key with usethis::edit_r_environ()
#    and restart R
# 2. Start a conversation: chat <- chat_openrouter(model = "anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5")
# 3. Ask it a question with chat$chat() and check you get an answer back

## What's in the chat object?

# Provider and model, number of turns, input and output tokens,
# and the user / assistant turns themselves
chat

## Counting tokens

# Totals for every call in this R session, across all chats
token_usage()

## Continuing the conversation

chat$chat("How long does this breed of dog usually live?")

# Input tokens went up: the whole conversation is sent every time
chat

## Reset - just start a new chat

chat <- chat_openrouter(model = "anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5")
chat$chat("What is its favourite food?")
# A new chat object has no history - the Labrador is gone

## Chatting interactively

chat <- chat_openrouter(model = "anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5")
live_console(chat)   # type Q to quit
live_browser(chat)

chat

## Your turn (2)

# 1. Start a new chat and open it with live_browser(chat)
# 2. Ask a few questions, including a follow-up that relies on an earlier answer
# 3. Close the browser window, then print chat - what do you see?

## Today's data: dog adoption listings

library(readr)
dogs <- read_csv("data/dogs.csv")
View(dogs)

## Giving the model something to work with

# chat$chat() takes any number of pieces of content and sends them together
boris <- dogs$description[1]

chat <- chat_openrouter(model = "anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5")
chat$chat("Give me a quick summary of this dog", boris)

## Your turn (3)

# 1. Pick a different dog from dogs and pass its description to chat$chat()
# 2. Ask: would this dog suit a flat with no garden?
# 3. Ask a follow-up question without repeating the description

# 0 - Welcome and Setup
# Using LLMs in R with ellmer - LatinR 2026

## Install the packages we'll use

install.packages(c("ellmer", "dplyr", "readr", "tidyr", "usethis"))

## Add your OpenRouter API key to .Renviron
## (you'll be given a key on the day; ask us if you haven't got one)

usethis::edit_r_environ()

# Add this line to the file that opens, save it, then restart R:
# OPENROUTER_API_KEY=your-key-here

## Check the key is picked up

Sys.getenv("OPENROUTER_API_KEY") != ""

## Check ellmer can talk to the provider

library(ellmer)
chat <- chat_openrouter(model = "anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5")
chat$chat("Say hello in one short sentence.")

title: Section 2: Prompt Engineering
text:
The script for this section of the workshop. Exercises are at the end, under Your turn.
Download 02-prompt-engineering.R View on GitHub


code/02-prompt-engineering.R

# 2 - Prompt Engineering (brief)
# Using LLMs in R with ellmer - LatinR 2026
# [OPTIONAL - cut if short on time; section 3 stands alone]

library(ellmer)
library(dplyr)

dogs <- readr::read_csv("data/dogs.csv")

dog_description <- dogs |>
  slice(1) |>
  pull(description)

dog_description

## Without guidance the LLM is chatty and inconsistent

chat <- chat_openrouter(model = "anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5")
chat$chat("Summarise this dog:", dog_description)

## A system prompt sets the ground rules for the whole conversation

prompt <- "You are a dog adoption assistant helping people find dogs to adopt.
Summarise the dog description you are given to help potential adopters decide
if the dog is a good fit for them. Respond in 50 words or fewer.

## Output format

Name: the dog's name
Summary: a 1 sentence description
Age group: one of Baby, Young, Adult, Senior
Likes and dislikes: what the dog does and doesn't enjoy"

chat <- chat_openrouter(
  model = "anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5",
  system_prompt = prompt
)
chat$chat("Summarise this dog:", dog_description)

## Run it again - the format holds, but the wording still varies

chat <- chat_openrouter(
  model = "anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5",
  system_prompt = prompt
)
chat$chat("Summarise this dog:", dog_description)

# Prompting gets you a long way: a role, a clear task, and an output format
# are usually enough. But the result is still free text we'd have to parse.
# In the next section we make the model return data instead.

## Your turn

# 1. Pick a different dog from the dataset and run the prompt on it
# 2. Add one more field to the output format that YOU would want to know
#    before adopting a dog

title: Section 4: Tool Calling
text:
The script for this section of the workshop. Exercises are at the end, under Your turn.
Download 04-tool-calling.R View on GitHub


code/04-tool-calling.R

# 4 - Tool Calling
# Using LLMs in R with ellmer - LatinR 2026

library(ellmer)
library(dplyr)

## Client-side vs server-side tools

# A tool is a function the model can ask to have run for it. There are two
# kinds:
#
# SERVER-SIDE tools run on the provider's infrastructure. The model calls
# them without R being involved. Web search is the most common example.
#
# CLIENT-SIDE tools are R functions on our machine. The model asks for them,
# ellmer runs them, and sends the result back to the model.

## Server-side: web search with ":online"

# Without search, the model only knows what it learned in training...
chat <- chat_openrouter(model = "anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5")
chat$chat("Which dog breeds are most popular this year?")

# ...with search, OpenRouter runs a web search before the model answers
chat <- chat_openrouter(model = "anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5:online")
chat$chat("Which dog breeds are most popular this year?")

# The search happened on the provider's side. There is no tool call for
# ellmer to run, so the turn just contains the answer
chat$last_turn()

## Client-side: your own R functions as tools

# Define the function
get_time <- function() {
  format(Sys.time(), "%A %d %B %Y, %H:%M")
}

# Create tool
time_tool <- tool(get_time, "Get the current date and time")

# Without the tool the model has to guess...
chat <- chat_openrouter(model = "anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5")
chat$chat("what date is it right now?")

# ...with the tool it asks ellmer to run our function
chat$register_tool(time_tool)
chat$chat("what date is it right now?")

# Print the chat to see the tool request and result in the history
chat

## Giving the model our dog database

# We don't need a tool to filter the data - we can just send the file
prompt <- "You are a dog adoption assistant helping the user choose a dog
from the listings they give you."

chat <- chat_openrouter(
  model = "anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5",
  system_prompt = prompt
)

chat$chat(
  "Here are the dogs available:",
  content_document_file("data/dogs_details.csv")
)
chat$chat("I live in a small flat and already have a dog. Which three would suit me?")

## A tool that changes things: save a shortlist to a file

# Define the function - note it returns a string describing what it did
save_shortlist <- function(names, path) {
  writeLines(names, path)
  paste("Saved", length(names), "dogs to", path)
}

# Create tool - this time with arguments the model has to supply
save_shortlist_tool <- tool(
  save_shortlist,
  "Save a shortlist of dog names to a text file",
  arguments = list(
    names = type_array(type_string("Dog names")),
    path = type_string("File path to save to")
  )
)

chat$register_tool(save_shortlist_tool)
chat$chat("Save those three to shortlist.txt")

readLines("shortlist.txt")

## Should the model be allowed to do that?

# Checking the time just reads something. Saving a file changes something on
# our machine, and we might want a say in that. Annotations let us describe
# what each tool does...
time_tool <- tool(
  get_time,
  "Get the current date and time",
  annotations = tool_annotations(read_only_hint = TRUE)
)

save_shortlist_tool <- tool(
  save_shortlist,
  "Save a shortlist of dog names to a text file",
  arguments = list(
    names = type_array(type_string("Dog names")),
    path = type_string("File path to save to")
  ),
  annotations = tool_annotations(read_only_hint = FALSE)
)

# ...and on_tool_request() runs before every tool call. Return nothing to
# allow it, or call tool_reject() to block it.
chat <- chat_openrouter(
  model = "anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5",
  system_prompt = prompt
)
chat$register_tool(time_tool)
chat$register_tool(save_shortlist_tool)

chat$on_tool_request(function(request) {
  # Read-only tools go straight through
  if (isTRUE(request@tool@annotations$read_only_hint)) {
    return()
  }

  cat("The model wants to run", request@name, "with arguments:\n")
  str(request@arguments)

  answer <- readline("Allow? (y/n) ")
  if (tolower(answer) != "y") {
    tool_reject("The user did not approve this action")
  }
})

chat$chat(
  "Here are the dogs available:",
  content_document_file("data/dogs_details.csv")
)

# Answer "n" when asked - the model is told why, and carries on gracefully
chat$chat("Pick two adult dogs and save them to adults.txt")
file.exists("adults.txt")

# Read-only tools don't trigger the question
chat$chat("what time is it?")

## Try it live

live_console(chat)

## Your turn

# 1. Ask the assistant to save a different shortlist, and approve it this time
# 2. Change the rule in on_tool_request() so saving is only ever allowed to
#    files ending in ".txt", without asking
# 3. Bonus: log every tool call (name and arguments) to a data frame using
#    on_tool_request(), so you can see what the model did during a chat

title: Using LLMs in R with ellmer
text:
by Nic Crane





Wednesday 11th November 2026, 08:30-12:00 COT (UTC-5), Sala 1
LatinR 2026, Universidad de Antioquia, Medellín, Colombia


Workshop Overview
LLMs can be massively useful in R workflows, when used in the right places and if you’re aware of not only the benefits, but also the risks. In this hands-on workshop, you’ll learn how to use LLMs programmatically in R, and come away with both the confidence to experiment and a working script that extracts data from unstructured text.
We’ll look at where LLMs can help, where they’ll let you down, and techniques for making your results more trustworthy. You’re going to leave with a practical sense of what’s possible and where to be cautious.
What you’ll learn:

Getting started with LLMs in R using {ellmer}
Prompt engineering for more predictable results
Extracting structured data from unstructured text
Using LLMs to call R functions (tool calling)



Workshop Prework

Environment
You’ll need an R environment to work in; this could be RStudio or Positron on your own laptop, or an account on Posit Cloud via a web browser.
If you’re on a work machine with restrictions on installing software or connecting to external APIs, Posit Cloud is a good option as everything runs in your browser.


Packages
Install the required packages:
install.packages(c("ellmer", "dplyr", "readr", "tidyr", "usethis"))


API keys
You’ll need an API key from an LLM provider. We’ll be using OpenRouter, and you will be sent a key on the day of the workshop. In section 1 we’ll add it to your .Renviron file as OPENROUTER_API_KEY.



Workshop Schedule

Section 0: Welcome and Setup
Section 1: Getting Started with LLMs in R
Section 2: Prompt Engineering (brief)
Section 3: Structured Output
Section 4: Tool Calling
Section 5 (bonus, time permitting): Other Libraries for Working with LLMs in R
Wrap-up and Resources



Instructor and TA
Nic Crane (instructor) is an R consultant with a background in data science and software engineering. They maintain the Apache Arrow R package and help maintain ellmer, and are passionate about open source, and learning and teaching all things R.
Yanina Bellini Saibene (TA) is Community Manager at rOpenSci, a 2026 Sovereign Tech Fellow, part of the RLadies+ Global leadership team, a board member of The Carpentries, and a co-founder of LatinR. Yani will be helping out with the exercises.
